Multiple train and ferry routes disrupted because of storm
published at 08:02 GMT
08:02 GMT
Image source,
National Rail says that Storm Boelo is affecting multiple train operators and routes across the country today, including:
Avanti West Coast advises to avoid travelling north of Preston
LNER warns against travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen
TransPennine Express says only travel if essential
ScotRail reports disruptions affecting 21 of its 39 routes
Transport for Wales says there are cancellations across several routes including Swansea and Shrewsbury
Some ferry operators are also impacted by the storm.
A Stena Line service between Belfast and Liverpool is cancelled due to "adverse weather conditions", with two more crossings to Cairnryan also cancelled
Almost all of the services operated by CalMac in Scotland are cancelled because of strong winds
NorthLink Ferries, also in Scotland, warns of the possibility of disruption through to Thursday, with several services are already cancelled
Stick with us throughout the day as we bring you more travel updates.

Almost 7cm of rain fell in 24 hours in some parts of UK
published at 07:54 GMT
07:54 GMT
Stormchaser AL / BBC Weather Watchers
Image caption,
These people in Dunster, Somerset, braved the wet weather on Saturday
As anyone in the UK will have noticed, Saturday was wet - with rain falling across the entire country at some point.
Figures from this morning show up to 7cm (2.7in) of rain fell in the previous 24 hours, with the highest amounts recorded at:
Liscombe (Somerset) 69.2mm
Tyndrum (Stirling) 66.4mm
Achnagart (Highland) 66.2mm
Shap (Cumbria) 60.6mm
Tulloch Bridge (Highland) 56.2mm
Cardiff Bute Park 55.2mm
Capel Curig (Conwy) 54.6mm
Winds not easing until overnight for north of UK as Scotland set for more heavy rain
published at 07:42 GMT
07:42 GMT
Louise Lear
BBC Weather
Rossi/BBC Weather Watchers
One weather watcher has sent in a picture of grey skies in Nairn, in the Highlands, which is currently under a yellow rain warning
The strongest winds have
generally been across the north west of the UK
, chiefly Scotland, where gusts of over 80mph have been recorded.
There were also strong winds further south, in fact 85mph on the Isle of Wight.
Most of the rain has now cleared southern parts, but many central and western areas will see showers today, and Scotland has further showers and heavy rain to come.
Winds remain strong this morning, easing in the south this afternoon and in the north overnight.
Scottish roads closed due to fallen trees and flooding
published at 07:30 GMT
07:30 GMT
Graham/BBC Weather Watchers
Fallen trees and flooding have been causing disruption on the roads in Scotland, with Traffic Scotland issuing a string of updates on social media.
It says several A roads remain closed in some areas, including:
The A82 at the Bridge of Orchy is closed in both directions due to fallen trees
The A84 in both directions at Runacraig due to a fallen tree
The A87 in both directions at Breakish due to a fallen tree
The A76 Drumlanrig in both directions due to a fallen tree
The A726 in both directions at Righead Roundabout due to a fallen tree
Sections of two motorways were also closed earlier but have since reopened:
The M74 motorway - which runs from Glasgow to the English border - was closed northbound between Junctions 7 and 6 due to a fallen tree
The M8 motorway - which connects Scotland's east and west coasts - was also closed at Junction 18 eastbound due to flooding
What you need to know about UK weather warnings
published at 07:15 GMT
07:15 GMT
When dangerous weather is forecast, a weather warning will be issued by the Met Office, the UK’s national weather service.
Weather warnings are given a colour – yellow, amber or red - with yellow being the lowest, and red the most serious. The colour assigned depends on a combination of two things: the impact the weather is likely to have and the likelihood of it happening.
Yellow warnings:
Are the ones you will see most often. They give you a heads up that severe weather is possible and to start planning for impacts to either travel, power or property
Amber warnings:
Mean travel disruption is more likely and there is a potential risk to life and property
Red warnings:
These are rare, and have only been issued a handful of times in recent years. They mean the Met Office believes that dangerous, potentially life-threatening weather is expected imminently and you should immediately take action to keep yourself and other safe
An example of a Met Office warning matrix. Here, the position of the tick indicates that a yellow weather warning would be issued
Yellow and amber weather warnings still in place
published at 07:03 GMT
07:03 GMT
As we've been reporting, several Met Office weather warnings are still in place from yesterday - with some in effect until the end of the day. Here's a summary of those warnings and their end times:
An amber warning for wind ending at 10:00 GMT today affecting County Antrim and County Londonderry in Northern Ireland
A yellow warning for wind ending at 12:00 affecting  all of Northern Ireland
A yellow warning for rain ending at 15:00 in Central, Tayside and Fife, Grampian, and the Highlands
An amber warning for wind ending at 21:00 is in place across most of Scotland, plus north east and west England, and Yorkshire and Humber
A yellow warning for wind ending at 21:00 affecting Scotland, including the Orkney Islands, north east and west England, Yorkshire, northern Wales, and the East Midlands

Storm Boelo brings top wind gust of 85mph
published at 06:49 GMT
06:49 GMT
Storm Boelo brought a top wind gust of 85mph to the Scottish village of Machrihanish in Argyll and Bute around midnight, with the same speed also recorded at Needles in the Isle of Wight on Saturday afternoon.
Here's a round-up of some of the strongest gusts recorded elsewhere:
Capel Curig: 84mph
Tiree: 82mph
Islay Port Ellen: 81mph
St Bees Head: 78mph
South Uist: 78mph
Orlock Head: 78mph

Travel disruption to continue today as Storm Boelo brought gusts of 85mph overnight
published at 06:40 GMT
06:40 GMT
Katie Williams
Live reporter
Amber wind warnings remain in force as Storm Boelo continues to bring wet and windy weather to the UK.
The Met Office says winds peaked overnight with gusts of 60-70mph affecting some northern parts of the UK.
Gusts in some exposed coastal spots topped 80mph, with the village of Machrihanish in Argyll and Bute recording 85mph.
Four wind warnings remain in place today - two amber and two yellow - affecting most of the northern half of the UK. A yellow rain warning is still in force over parts of the Scottish Highlands.
A rain warning which stretched down to the southern part of the UK yesterday has lifted overnight.
The storm continues to disrupt transport, with Avanti West Coast advising against travelling north of Preston and LNER advising against travel between Edinburgh and Aberdeen.
Cumbria Police says it received "a number of calls overnight to localised flooding and fallen trees blocking roads".
There are also 14 active flood warnings currently in place from the Environment Agency, affecting areas such as Cumbria, Merseyside and the prime minister's constituency of Makerfield.
We'll bring you updates throughout the day - stick with us.
Second storm in two days brings travel disruption across UK
published at 18:16 BST 24 October
18:16 BST 24 October
Getty Images
The second storm in two days has brought wet and windy weather to the UK, causing travel disruption and event cancellations.
Scotland, Northern Ireland and the north of England are bracing for the worst of Storm Boelo, with gusts of up to 80mph forecast.
Three yellow weather warnings are already in place for wind and rain, impacting areas from Scotland right down to southern England.
Another three warnings will kick in this evening from 21:00, including two more serious amber warnings for wind impacting Northern Ireland, Scotland and northern England.
We've got full details on those here.
Halloween events have been cancelled in Scotland and Northern Ireland, a marathon has been called off in North Wales and Knowsley Safari Park in Merseyside, north-west England,
will be closed tomorrow.
National Rail has announced disruption on a number of lines,
flights to and from Dublin Airport
have been cancelled, and highway authorities are urging drivers to take particular care and avoid non-essential journeys.
A number of power cuts in the Glasgow and Edinburgh areas have already been reported to SP Energy Networks, while power outages continue to affect large parts of south-west England following Friday's Storm Austen.
We're pausing our live coverage now, but you can read the latest in
our news story.
